title: Build for the summer
translation: Build your house for the summer. In winter you can live anywhere. But a house that's bad in the hot season is unbearable.

In the garden, deep water doesn't look cool. A shallow stream looks far cooler. For reading or fine work, a room with sliding doors is brighter than one with lattice shutters. A high ceiling makes the room cold in winter and the lamps dim. And when you build, put in a space that has no particular use. It's nice to look at, and it turns out to be handy for all sorts of things.
People were talking it over once, and that's what they agreed on.
original: {家|いへ}のつくりやうは{夏|なつ}をむねとすべし。
{冬|ふゆ}はいかなる{所|ところ}にも{住|す}まる。
{暑|あつ}き{頃|ころ}わろき{住居|すまひ}は{堪|た}へがたきことなり。
{深|ふか}き{水|みづ}は{涼|すず}しげなし、{浅|あさ}くて{流|なが}れたる、{遥|はる}かに{涼|すず}し。
{細|こま}かなるものを{見|み}るに、{遣戸|やりど}は{蔀|しとみ}の{間|ま}よりもあかし。
{天井|てんじやう}の{高|たか}きは、{冬|ふゆ}{寒|さむ}く、{灯|ともしび}くらし。
{造作|ざうさく}は{用|よう}なき{所|ところ}をつくりたる、{見|み}るもおもしろく、よろづの{用|よう}にも{立|た}ちてよし。」とぞ、{人|ひと}のさだめあひ{侍|はべ}りし。
literal: The way of building a house should take summer as the main thing.
In winter one can live in any kind of place.
A bad dwelling in the hot season is unbearable.
Deep water does not look cool; shallow, flowing (water) is far cooler.
When looking at fine things, (a room with) sliding doors is brighter than a room with lattice shutters.
A high ceiling is cold in winter, and the lamps are dim.
As for the fittings, making a part that has no use is pleasant to look at and good, as it serves all kinds of purposes': so people decided together.

notes.text: むね: 'the main thing'. べし: 'should'. One of the best-known lines of the book, still quoted today to explain traditional Japanese houses: open, raised off the ground, with walls that slide away to let the air through.

notes.quote: 遣戸は蔀の間よりもあかし
notes.text: {遣戸|やりど}: a sliding door (the 1925 edition: 'a door you open sideways'). {蔀|しとみ}: a lattice shutter hinged at the top and propped up to open.
The light of a single oil lamp does not reach a high ceiling, so the room looks dark.

notes.quote: 造作は用なき所をつくりたる
notes.text: {造作|ざうさく}: the fittings of a house, doors, shelves, built-in parts (the 1925 edition: 'fixtures'). A space with no fixed purpose ends up used for everything.

notes.quote: 」とぞ、人のさだめあひ侍りし
notes.text: The section closes a quotation that it never opened: only here do you learn that everything before was what people said in a discussion. The 1925 edition prints it this way, and the translation follows. ぞ … し: き becomes し, and き shows that Kenkō was there.
